cards.headline: Bus services in Tampines to be fully handed over to Go-Ahead Singapore on July 19
bullets: Go-Ahead Singapore will run all 29 bus services in Tampines from July 19.
This includes 15 services previously run by SBS Transit.
The new services will use buses from the East Coast Integrated Depot.
Most SBS Transit staff will join Go-Ahead Singapore.

cards.headline: Three new Circle Line stations draw early morning crowds on opening day
bullets: Three new Circle Line MRT stations opened on July 12, with early birds catching the first trains.
Keppel, Cantonment, and Prince Edward Road stations now complete the Circle Line loop.
The new stations are expected to shorten travel times for many commuters.
Cantonment station features designs inspired by the old Tanjong Pagar Railway Station.

cards.headline: S’pore, M’sia partnership driven by mutual respect, understanding of each other’s interests: Tharman
bullets: Singapore and Malaysia work through disagreements to strengthen their overall partnership.
President Tharman says the relationship is built on mutual respect, not just transactions.
Both countries aim to resolve sensitive issues calmly and with international law.
Trust between leaders and people allows disputes to be managed through dialogue.
Joint projects like the Johor-Singapore SEZ and RTS Link show win-win cooperation.

cards.headline: President Tharman Shanmugaratnam to make first state visit to Malaysia
bullets: President Tharman will visit Malaysia from July 12 to 15.
This is his first state visit to Malaysia as President.
He will meet the Malaysian King and Prime Minister.
The President will also visit Kuala Lumpur and Selangor.

cards.headline: An ‘AI-resilient’ job doesn’t mean AI-free, say workers who use it to complement physical work
bullets: Healthcare workers and plumbers use AI to help with paperwork and planning, not replace their jobs.
Jobs needing human touch, like caring for the elderly, are seen as safe from AI replacement.
Workers in essential jobs feel pressure to learn AI tools to stay relevant.
AI can help skilled tradespeople with tasks like writing quotes and reports.
Some workers use AI to translate languages or create marketing materials.

cards.headline: President Tharman to make first state visit to Malaysia
bullets: President Tharman will make his first state visit to Malaysia from July 12 to 15.
He will meet Malaysia's King Sultan Ibrahim and Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
The President will also visit Selangor and meet its Sultan and Chief Minister.
He will attend events with business leaders and overseas Singaporeans.

cards.headline: WhatsApp reserves high-profile usernames ahead of privacy feature rollout, Singapore leaders' names blocked
bullets: WhatsApp blocked Singapore leaders' names like @LawrenceWong and @KShanmugam for its new username feature.
The new feature lets users chat without sharing phone numbers, aiming to stop impersonation.
Variations of these leaders' names were also reserved to prevent misuse.
This privacy update is rolling out globally, with users to be notified when it's available.

cards.headline: Several flights from Singapore cancelled as Typhoon Bavi takes aim at Taiwan and China
bullets: Typhoon Bavi caused several flights between Singapore and Taipei to be cancelled.
Singapore Airlines cancelled ten flights to and from Shanghai due to the typhoon.
The storm is one of the biggest to hit Taiwan in over 30 years.
Typhoon Bavi has already caused landslides and deaths in the Philippines.
Taiwan evacuated thousands and shut businesses as the typhoon approached.

cards.headline: Life as a football fan’s wife: I still don’t get offside, but I understand why it’s ‘the people’s game’
bullets: Being married to a football fan means caring about match results even without knowing the rules.
Many wives learn football terms and team details to connect with their partners.
Supporting a spouse's team can shift your own loyalties, even if you don't fully understand the game.
A team's win or loss can significantly impact the mood at home.
Football's social side and underdog stories make it enjoyable for non-fans too.

cards.headline: They shut themselves away for years. Now these hidden youth are trying to return to the world
bullets: A documentary series called Shutdown shows young people trying to rejoin society after years of isolation.
These 'hidden youth' withdraw due to fear and anxiety, not laziness.
One youth, Danzel, slept days, gamed nights, and needed physiotherapy after years inside.
Fei Yue Community Services sees over 111 cases, with 60 more on a waitlist.

cards.headline: Lexus ES 350e review: They bulked it up for one sad reason
bullets: The new electric Lexus ES 350e costs S$402,800 and is longer than BMW i5 or Mercedes E-Class.
It offers a very quiet and smooth ride, feeling like a luxury car.
The car has a spacious back seat with lots of legroom.
Some features like a panoramic roof and reclining rear seats are missing in the Singapore model.
Charging speed is slower compared to rivals from China and Germany.

cards.headline: AI office demand seen spreading beyond NYC, San Francisco
bullets: AI firms are looking for 37% bigger offices than other tech companies.
Office tours by AI tenants in the US jumped 85% in the past year.
AI office demand is expected to spread beyond New York and San Francisco.
Seattle, Chicago, and Washington are seeing early signs of AI growth.
AI companies are helping the office market recover from pandemic lows.

cards.headline: BT longevity forum turns the spotlight on health and wealth
bullets: Singaporeans now live about 10 years longer than the world average.
Life expectancy here reached 83.9 years in 2025.
Many may spend nearly a decade managing health issues after retirement.
A forum will discuss how to stay healthy and financially secure longer.
Speakers will share tips on health, wealth, and finding purpose in later life.

cards.headline: Deloitte Singapore set to move out of Shenton Way base to Orchard Central in 2027
bullets: Deloitte will move from Shenton Way to Orchard Central in 2027.
The company is moving after its current lease ends in late 2026.
Deloitte will occupy several floors in the upper levels of Orchard Central.
In the meantime, Deloitte will use a co-working space in Orchard.

cards.headline: Italian aristocrat sells pair of Neil Road shophouses for S$40.88 million
bullets: Two Neil Road shophouses sold for S$40.88 million.
The properties were bought in 2011 for S$17.5 million.
The new owner is a subsidiary of Aw & Sons Capital.
The shophouses are currently home to the Goethe-Institut.

cards.headline: 4 taken to hospital after getting stung by hornets near Redhill Market
bullets: Four people were taken to hospital after being stung by hornets near Redhill Market.
The hornets apparently came from a large hive found on a nearby tree.
One woman, in her 70s, suffered the worst injuries with swollen, bleeding ears.
The hornet nest has since been removed by pest control.

cards.headline: Elderly person filmed defecating into planter at S'pore community garden
bullets: An elderly person was filmed defecating in a community garden planter.
The video was posted online and caused a debate about public hygiene and compassion.
The National Environment Agency stated that public defecation is an offence.
The person who filmed the incident reported it via the OneService app.

cards.headline: WhatsApp usernames of S’pore politicians like Lawrence Wong & Lee Hsien Loong already locked down to prevent impersonation
bullets: WhatsApp locked usernames for Singapore leaders like Lawrence Wong to stop impersonators.
This includes variations of their names to prevent fake accounts.
The feature lets users hide phone numbers and be found by username.
Politicians' usernames are secured before the feature officially launches.

cards.headline: 8 Dreamy Places In Singapore That Look Like A Studio Ghibli Film Come To Life
bullets: Jurong Lake Gardens has grassy hills that look like a scene from Howl's Moving Castle.
The Lorong Halus Red Bridge offers views similar to Spirited Away and is known for ghost sightings.
The Buddha Tooth Relic Temple in Chinatown resembles the bathhouse from Spirited Away.
Little Guilin's calm waters and cliffs are like the enchanted lake in Princess Mononoke.
The Tembusu tree in Botanic Gardens looks like the tree where Totoro sits.

cards.headline: 11 Best SG61 Deals To Celebrate National Day With, Like 1-For-1 Buffets & SG-Inspired Bites
bullets: Permata offers 1-for-1 buffet deals for lunch and dinner until August 31.
Swensen's has a $61 family set meal and new local-inspired dishes.
Guzman y Gomez brings back butter chicken filling and an advent calendar.
Tonkatsu ENbiton and Tamago-EN offer freebies with $61 spending.
Eu Yan Sang has deals with discounts up to 61%.
